0.long_answer: Diethylstilbestrol (DES) is the synthetic estrogen that was formerly used to treat female hypogonadism. DES was once widely prescribed for a range of indications including estrogen deficiency and as a preventive measure for pregnancy complications. However, it was later associated with severe reproductive health complications in individuals exposed to it in utero, including an increased risk of clear cell carcinoma and other reproductive tract abnormalities. As a result, its clinical use was discontinued.
